Isolate the trigonometric term and take the inverse tangent:
$$3\tan(2x + 1) = 1 \implies \tan(2x + 1) = \frac{1}{3}$$
$$2x + 1 = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \approx 0.32175\text{ radians}$$

Since $x > 0 \implies 2x + 1 > 1$, add integer multiples of $\pi$ to obtain valid positive arguments:
$$2x_1 + 1 = 0.32175 + \pi \approx 3.46334 \implies 2x_1 = 2.46334 \implies x_1 \approx 1.2317 \approx 1.23\text{ radians}$$
$$2x_2 + 1 = 0.32175 + 2\pi \approx 6.60494 \implies 2x_2 = 5.60494 \implies x_2 \approx 2.8025 \approx 2.80\text{ radians}$$
$$(\text{Smallest two positive values: } x = 1.23, \quad 2.80)$$

Use the identity $\sin^2 x = 1 - \cos^2 x$ to rewrite $f(x)$:
$$f(x) = 3 - 5\sin^2 x = 3 - 5(1 - \cos^2 x) = 3 - 5 + 5\cos^2 x = 5\cos^2 x - 2$$
where $a = 5$ and $b = -2$.

hints: Since $0 \le \cos^2 x \le 1$, evaluate $f(x)$ bounds from $5(0) - 2 = -2$ to $5(1) - 2 = 3$.
walkthrough:
Determine the extrema of $f(x) = 5\cos^2 x - 2$ on $0 \le x \le \pi$ (where $0 \le \cos^2 x \le 1$):
$$\text{Minimum value} = 5(0) - 2 = -2$$
$$\text{Maximum value} = 5(1) - 2 = 3$$
$$\text{Range of } f: \quad -2 \le f(x) \le 3 \quad (\text{or } [-2, 3])$$
